summary: The reading that follows a rename no longer takes the selection from an item that was selected in the meantime. All in src/finder. `submit_rename` (dialogs.rs) calls the new `load_listing_renamed(was, now)` in place of `load_listing(vec![target], true)`. In mod.rs `load_listing` is a wrapper around `load_listing_unless(select, renamed_from, quiet)`. With `renamed_from`, its completion collects, before `rebuild_rows`, the paths selected among the rows other than the old name (new `selected_among_rows()`: the rows' selection, or in the column view the first column's item while that column is the one in use), and after `rebuild_rows` selects the renamed item only when none of them is still selected, which is to say still listed. `renamed_in_columns` calls `load_column_unless(.., gives_way = true)`, whose completion selects the renamed item only when `kept.is_none() && this.active_column >= col`; `load_column` is its wrapper with `false`. The 15 other callers of `load_listing` and the 3 of `load_column` are untouched, so a paste, Undo and the Trash keep the present rule. docs/manual.md: one sentence in the Rename… row.
changelog: Ending a rename with a click or a right-click on another item selected the renamed item again a moment later. The menu that the right-click had opened then acted on the renamed item, not on the item it named, so its Move to Trash moved the file just renamed to the Trash, and after a click the next key did the same. A name edited in the sidebar's tree and ended on a file did this with the folder, and so did a folder renamed among a search's results when the click was on a result inside it. The item pressed now stays selected, an arrow key pressed right after Return is no longer undone, and renaming a folder in the sidebar's tree no longer takes the selection from the items selected among the files.
behaviour_changes: List, icon view and search results: a rename ended by a click or a right-click on another item leaves that item selected. The menu the right-click opened acts on the item it names, and a key after a click acts on the item clicked. Before, the renamed item was selected again once its folder had been read, and Move to Trash or Cmd+Backspace hit the file just renamed. Tested (list right-click and Move to Trash, icon view click and Cmd+Backspace, search results), and pictured.

Column view, in the first column and in a further one: the same. A click on the folder's own row, a column back, now leaves that column in use with the folder selected. Before, the renamed item's column was in use again. Tested, and pictured.

A key that selects another item right after Return, before the folder has been read again, is no longer undone. Tested for Up in the list; probed by the implementer for Down in the first column and Left in a further column.
New Folder, named and ended by a press on another item: that item stays selected. Before, the new folder was. Probed by the implementer.
A Cmd- or Shift-click that ends an edit keeps what it selected, less the renamed item ([Roadmap.md] where the trunk had [plan.txt]). Probed.

A name edited in the sidebar's tree, with the folder listed among the files: a file pressed to end the edit stays selected, whether or not it was selected before, and its menu acts on it (before: the folder was selected among the files, and the file's menu moved the folder to the Trash). With other items selected among the files, or in the first column while it is in use, Return leaves them selected, where the folder used to take the selection. With nothing else selected, or the folder itself selected, the folder is selected under its new name, as before. Tested. By reading, the same holds for a folder made and named in the tree with New Folder.

Search results, a folder renamed among them (or in the sidebar's tree) and the name ended by a press on a result inside that folder: the result stays selected (the review's fix). Before, on the trunk and on the implementer's commit, the folder was selected again under a menu that read Cut “Project Atlas.txt”, and Move to Trash moved the whole folder to the Trash. Such a result is listed under the path it had until the search runs again, so its Move to Trash finds no file, says “Couldn’t move to the Trash”, and its row goes; the folder and the file stay. Tested, and pictured before and after.
When the pressed item stays selected, the view no longer scrolls to the renamed item's new place.

Unchanged: Return, a press on the status bar or on empty space, and the gallery's dialog (also during a search) select the renamed item; Return then Escape in a column selects it again; New Folder named with a further column in use; a double-click on a folder during an edit; a press on an item inside the renamed folder, in a folder open in the list or in the column to its right, selects the folder (see left_out). The implementer probed each on the trunk's source and on the commit. The final code differs from the commit only where a selected item is no longer listed after the reading, and the review probed again on it: Return among a search's results, the gallery's dialog during a search, and the press inside the renamed folder in the list and in the columns.
Manual, the Rename… row: the item is selected under its new name afterward, unless the click was on another item, which is selected then, with the menu a right-click opens.
left_out: A press on an item inside the folder whose name is being edited still ends with the folder selected, as on the trunk: in a folder open in place in the list (the folder is closed under its new name, and the item's row has gone), and in the column to the folder's right, in the first or a further column. No menu is drawn after such a right-click (probed again in review), and Cmd+Backspace after such a click moves the whole folder to the Trash, with the highlight showing the folder. Keeping the item selected means carrying the selection, the open column and the list's `expanded` set over to the new path, which is a change of its own. a_press_inside_a_folder_that_ends_its_rename_leaves_the_folder_selected pins the present behaviour.

A Cmd- or Shift-click that ends an edit drops the renamed item from the selection, and so does Return for a folder renamed in the tree while it is one of several items selected among the files. Keeping it would mean putting the new name into the selection in the old one's place (a `Selection` method that adds an item without moving the cursor).

In the gallery during a search, rows made again between the dialog's Rename and the end of the reading (a quiet search answering, sizes arriving) leave the gallery on its first item, not on the renamed one: the first item, which the gallery picked itself, then counts as another item. The reading takes milliseconds on a local disk. No test; a probe of gallery plus search plus Return selects the renamed result.
No pictures of the tree and Select All cases: the screenshot example has no step that reaches a tree row's Rename…. They are covered by tests.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: nothing in src/term is touched, and grep finds no use there, in src/macos.rs, src/win.rs, examples or crates, of any function changed.
Nothing was compiled or run on macOS or Windows. No cfg-gated code is touched.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message. README.md says nothing this changes.

review_fixes: Found with a probe and fixed: the fault was still there among a search's results. The implementer's rule for the rows was "an item is selected that is neither the old name nor inside it", so that a press on an item inside a folder open in the list would leave the folder selected, as before. Among a search's results an item inside the renamed folder keeps its row. With a folder renamed there (or in the sidebar's tree) and the name ended by a right-click on a result inside it, the folder was selected again under a menu that read Cut “Project Atlas.txt”, and Move to Trash moved the folder with everything in it to the Trash; a click and Cmd+Backspace did the same. The trunk does this too, so it was the brief's fault left in, not a new one. The rule is now "another item is selected among the rows as the reading ends, and is still listed after it": `selected_besides(path) -> bool` became `selected_among_rows() -> Vec<&Path>`, asked before `rebuild_rows` (for what else is selected) and after it (for whether any of that is still selected). In the list an item inside the renamed folder is no longer listed, so the folder is selected as before and the implementer's guard test passes unchanged; among results the item stays selected. Test: the second block of a_click_on_another_result_that_ends_a_rename_leaves_that_result_selected, seen failing on the implementer's commit and on the trunk's source.
The commit message says the rule as it is now, and names the search results' case in its first paragraph and in the changelog entry.

/home/user/polish-tools/shots/fix-rename-press-selection-mutations.py is rewritten for the code as it went to the trunk (eleven mutations, with what each fails), and the reviewer's probes with what they printed are appended to fix-rename-press-selection-probes.txt.

Rebased twice while integrating, each time without a conflict: onto 5e68c44, which brought ffb02de (fix-own-small-faults) and 5e68c44 (fix-filter-reruns-and-fresh-rows), and then onto a085120 (fix-here-folder-spelling), which landed while the check ran. check.sh was run again after each. None of the three touches the code of a rename's reading: fix-own-small-faults' guard for the buttons under the file area's message stops a press only where no row is drawn, and fix-filter-reruns-and-fresh-rows adds one more place that makes a search's rows again between a rename and the end of its reading (a quiet search that brings a row another size or date), which matters only for the gallery's case under left_out.
notes:
Checked. With the implementer's src diff reverse-applied on ddefe96 the four tests that are to fail do, each for the brief's reason (basics: plan.txt where Roadmap.md was pressed, in the list and in the first column; finder: Atlas Plan.txt where Atlas Notes.txt was clicked; folder_tree: Work where notes.txt was pressed), and the four guards pass; applied again, `git status` was clean. The block added in review fails on the implementer's commit (maps where the result inside it was pressed). Eleven mutations of the final code, one at a time: ten each fail the test that is there for them and no other (always-select: the four main tests; what else is selected asked after the rows are made again: the gallery's dialog; an item counted whether or not it is still listed: the list block of a_press_inside…; the implementer's rule: the review's block; the first column asked whichever column is in use: the New Folder guard; the other views' selection asked in the column view: the Select All block; four of a further column's rule: the blocks of the two column tests). The eleventh, the old name not left out of what else is selected, fails no test: the old name is no longer listed once the folder has been read, so leaving it out matters only where it still is by then (a search that ran again meanwhile on an index that had seen the new name and not yet lost the old one, a file another program made under the old name). It is left out all the same. The 24 tests around renaming in the four test files pass with SEED=3, 11, 77, 2026, 4242 and 31337. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the amended commit on ddefe96 (816 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures), on 5e68c44 after the first rebase (827 passed), and on the trunk commit, 4efa254 on a085120 (834 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures). I looked at the window myself: the list after F2, a new name and a right-click on another row (that row selected under its own menu, the status bar counting it); the same in the first column (light) and in a further column (dark); and a search's results with a folder renamed among them and a right-click on a result inside it, on the implementer's commit (the folder selected and at the end of the path bar under a menu that reads Cut “Project Atlas.txt”) and on the final code (the result selected).

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the runs say. (1) A command still landing on an item the user didn't press. That was real: see review_fixes, the first. With it fixed I went through everything a press can land on while a name is edited. An item that is selected by the press, or was selected already, is among the rows' selection or the column's, and the reading gives way to it wherever its row or its column's row is still there afterwards; the choice is made when the reading ends, which is always after the press has been dealt with (the reading's answer waits for the event that ended the edit), and I ran the order a real click has, with the reading answering between the press and the release of the mouse, for a right and a left click. What remains is an item whose row goes with the rename (inside the renamed folder, left_out) and the grey row of an earlier column, whose right-click selects nothing (column-row-menu-wrong-item, there before). (2) Return no longer selecting the renamed item, so that the next key acts on nothing or on something else. The old name is left out of what else is selected, and is gone from the rows once they are made again, so with nothing else selected the item is selected as it was: tested in the list, the icon view, both kinds of column, the gallery's dialog, New Folder in the list and in the columns, after Select All in the column view, and probed for a search's results (a folder and a file) and the gallery's dialog during a search. The one case that differs is a name edited in the sidebar's tree with other items selected among the files (doubt a). (3) The column view and the other views' selection coming apart, or the keyboard ending in the wrong place. Where the reading gives way it changes nothing: the rows' selection is only remapped by path, the columns stay as the press left them, nothing is scrolled, and the keyboard is where the press or the end of the edit put it (the files after a press on an item, the tree after Return in the tree). `select_row_in_columns` still runs only inside the branch that selects.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) A name edited in the sidebar's tree and ended with Return no longer moves the selection among the files to the folder when other items are selected there. That is deliberate, and follows from the rule: a right-click on a file that is selected already selects nothing new, so by the selection it can't be told from Return, and going by a change of the selection (the lane's first attempt) left the fault for exactly that press. The keyboard is in the tree after such a rename, so no file key acts on the files' selection then. If the folder should take the selection after Return all the same, the press needs a signal of its own; the last block of a_press_on_a_file_that_ends_a_rename_in_the_tree… turns around. (b) A press on an item inside the folder being renamed still selects the folder (left_out, the first). The highlight shows the folder, and no menu is drawn, so nothing is named that isn't acted on; but a click on a file in the folder's column and then Cmd+Backspace moves the folder to the Trash. (c) A result inside a folder renamed here now stays selected under a path that is gone, and its commands fail with a notification, where the folder used to be selected and the commands hit it. The better end is for such results to follow the rename (Found, not fixed). (d) The gallery during a search (left_out, the third). (e) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows.

For briefs still to come.
- column-row-menu-wrong-item: the rename's reading of a further column (`load_column_unless` with `gives_way`) leaves the renamed item unselected when a column before it is the one in use as the reading ends (`this.active_column >= col` is false), or when another item is selected in that column. If your right-press on the grey row of an earlier column makes that column the one in use, a rename in a further column ended by that press ends as the click on the folder's own row does in the third block of a_press_on_another_row_that_ends_a_rename_leaves_that_row_selected_in_its_column: that column in use, the folder selected, its column read again with nothing selected. For the first column the rows' rule asks `selected_among_rows()`, which is the first column's item only while `active_column == 0` at the end of the reading; a press that makes the first column the one in use without selecting is seen there. Not probed here: a rename in a further column ended by a right-click on the already selected row of an earlier column.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: `load_listing`'s completion is now in `load_listing_unless`, and for a rename it reads `selected_among_rows()` before and after `rebuild_rows`: the rows' selection, or in the column view the first column's `selected` while that column is in use. `select_row_in_columns` is called as before, inside the branch that selects. If `set_view_mode` comes to select in the first column, a view chosen between a rename and the end of its reading is read as the column shows it then.
- select-all-perf: for a rename's reading only (`renamed_from` is `Some`), the completion clones the path of every selected row but the old name into a `HashSet<PathBuf>`, and when that set isn't empty asks `selected_among_rows()` (a `Vec<&Path>` of the selected rows) once more after `rebuild_rows`. With every item selected and a name edited in the sidebar's tree that is one clone per selected item per rename. Any other reading builds an empty set and asks nothing.
- files-changed-off-thread: `files_changed` still calls `load_listing(here, true, cx)`, the wrapper, with the present rule: what a paste, Undo or the Trash brings is selected whatever is selected by then. `submit_rename` doesn't go through `files_changed`.
- filter-stale-keep-set: a_click_that_ends_a_name_under_a_filter_selects_the_item_clicked now also asserts, after its last settle, that the result clicked is still selected once the filter has answered for the new name. The rename's reading gives way to an item that is selected and still listed, so the line holds whether or not a renamed result's row stays listed until its run answers.
- icon-tile-hit-target: a_press_on_another_item_that_ends_a_rename_leaves_that_item_selected clicks the middle of a tile (`item_id("tile", ..)`) to end an edit and then presses Cmd+Backspace. The click has to land on the item: in empty space it would clear the selection, and the renamed item would be selected again.
- context-menus-fit: the new tests read `Cut “Roadmap.md”` and `Cut “Atlas Plan.txt”` among an item's menu labels and click `Move to Trash`, and the tree's `Rename…`, by label, at the menu's top level.
- quick-look-empty-state, preview-page-keys: the reading's completion still ends with `selection_changed(cx)`, whether or not it selected.
- restore-session-tabs: `load_listing(select, quiet, cx)` keeps its signature.
- idle-redraw-after-search, split-active-pane, inactive-selection-colour, type-select-space, go-to-folder-keyboard, recents-walk-index, collapsible-sidebar-sections, tree-arrows-past-smart-folder: independent.

Found, not fixed (there before this change, outside this brief).
- A press on an item inside the folder whose name is being edited selects the folder (left_out, the first). The same with a key: Return on a folder's new name in a column and then Right goes into the folder's column, and is taken back when the column is read again (by reading).
- Results inside a folder that is renamed in the window keep their old paths: `submit_rename` puts the new path only in the result that was renamed. They stay listed until the search runs again, which the index's report of the rename doesn't bring about, a rename made here not being searched for again. Probed: after the report and two looks the row is still there, and Return hands the old path to the system; Move to Trash says “Couldn’t move to the Trash” and drops the row.
- A name changed inside a folder that is open in the list keeps showing the old name until the next two-second look, and nothing is selected after that: `submit_rename` reads the window's folder and a further column again, not the list's `children`. Probed by the implementer and again in review.
- A folder open in the list is closed after its rename (`expanded` keeps the old path).
- Recents lists a file under its old name after a rename there until the index has seen it, and the file isn't selected after that: the rename's reading finds no row for the new name. Probed in the test harness, whose index doesn't watch.
- A right-click that ends an edit draws no menu when the row pressed moves from under the pointer as the folder is read again (the new name sorts across it, or New Folder was named above it): the kit draws a menu only while its row is under the point pressed. The item pressed is selected.
- A right-click on another row while a refused name is still being edited selects that row and opens its menu: `right_click_row` and the column's right-press have no check of `renaming`, as `click_row` has. By reading.
- A right-click on the grey row of an earlier column opens the menu of the column in use's item (column-row-menu-wrong-item, already a brief).
